invariants.text: A customer can have multiple orders.
An order cannot exist without a corresponding customer.
An order must belong to exactly one customer.
Customer.customer_id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
Customer.email must be a string
Customer.email must not be null
Customer.name must be a string
Customer.name must not be null
Each customer must have a unique customer_id that identifies them within the system.
Each order has a status that reflects its current state in the order lifecycle.
Each order must have a unique order_id that identifies it within the system.
Order.customer_id must be an integer
Order.customer_id must not be null
Order.customer_id must reference an existing Customer.customer_id
Order.order_date must be a datetime
Order.order_date must not be null
Order.order_id must be an auto-incremented integer primary key with default value None
Order.status must be a string
Order.status must not be null
The order date must be set when an order is created and cannot be modified after creation.
The order_date of an order must be on or after the system's current date when the order is created.
The status of an order can only be updated through a dedicated update operation and must be one of the valid status values defined in the system.
When a customer is listed, all orders associated with that customer must be returned in the list response.
